title: Graceful Backout Recommender with Simulated Traffic Replay
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build an automated backout recommendation system that runs a low-risk simulated traffic replay against candidate config changes (batching, caching, and routing policies) and outputs a calibrated backout score plus a contextual rationale and remediation steps. The system should surface both cost and correctness signals, prioritize safe rollbacks for changes that cause token-cost regressions or cache thrash, and produce human-readable runbook steps for on-call or automated actuators.
tasks: Design and implement a lightweight traffic replayer that can consume recent anonymized request traces and replay at reduced scale against a candidate config in a sandboxed runtime
Map telemetry signals to scoring inputs: latency p95/p99, tail token cost per request, batch utilization, KV cache hit rate, model fallback/variant rate, error rate, and request queue depth
Implement cost-correctness backout scoring model and thresholds with configurable hysteresis; include a conservative default for production apps
Integrate simulated replay flow into the config apply pipeline: pre-apply simulation, post-apply quick-check, and continuous monitor with automated suggestion to backout
Add UI/console panel that shows a replay summary, score breakdown, and one-click backout recommendation with proposed rollback target and warmup plan
Create automated actuator prototype for safe backout (dry-run + staged swap) and a manual runbook for on-call
Add e2e tests: synthetic load scenarios (high-batching, cold-cache), failure modes (KV eviction storms), and golden comparisons against baseline configs
Instrument rollout to Dedicated canary pool first, run 2-weeks of monitored experiments, and collect false-positive/false-negative telemetry
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can replay a 1-hour anonymized traffic slice at 5x speed in sandbox without impacting production
Backout score correlates with observed production regressions: in 80% of simulated regressions (latency or cost > 15% from baseline) the system recommends backout
Console surface displays per-signal contribution to score and a clear remediation plan (rollback target and warmup steps)
Automated actuator performs staged swap rollback in canary pool and validates warmup before traffic shift
No customer-facing incidents caused by simulator runs; privacy-preserving replay pipeline meets data retention policy
notes: Motivation: many recent cost regressions emerged after batching/caching tuning. Existing change-safeguards trigger on error rates but miss economic regressions caused by inefficient batching or cache misconfigurations.

Design trade-offs: replay fidelity vs safety. We intentionally run reduced-scale replay and conservative thresholds to avoid noisy false positives. Final thresholds will be tuned during the canary window.
Privacy: replay uses anonymized payloads and strips PII; consult Legal for one-time signoff on stored traces for repro purposes.
Future: output could feed Redwood Optimize to suggest alternative batching/quantization presets when backout is recommended due to cost
